title: Pseudo-coherent complexes lift from a quasi-compact open of an affine scheme
statement: Let X be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] and U a quasi-compact open subscheme of X. For every pseudo-coherent object E of D(\mathcal O_U) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex], there exists a bounded-above complex of finite free \mathcal O_X-modules whose restriction to U is isomorphic to E in D(\mathcal O_U).

proof.text: By [lem-sc-pseudo-coherent-qcoh], E belongs to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_U). The quasi-compact-open lifting lemma [lem-sc-qc-open-derived-lift] gives E' in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X) with E'|_U\cong E.

Write X=\operatorname{Spec}(A). By the affine derived equivalence [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence], choose a complex M^\bullet of A-modules whose associated complex represents E'. Choose f_1,\ldots,f_r\in A with U=\bigcup_jD(f_j). On D(f_j)=\operatorname{Spec}(A_{f_j}) the object E'|_{D(f_j)}\cong E|_{D(f_j)} is pseudo-coherent (pseudo-coherence is local [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex]) and is represented by \widetilde{M^\bullet_{f_j}} (localization is exact). Applying the affine pseudo-coherence criterion [lem-pc-affine-pseudo-coherent-criterion] over A_{f_j}, each M^\bullet_{f_j} is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded-above complex of finite free A_{f_j}-modules.

source.place: Tag 08EE proof, X=Spec(A), choice of M and finite principal-open cover

proof.text: Construct by descending induction on n a complex F^\bullet of finite free A-modules, bounded above, and a map of complexes \alpha:F^\bullet\to M^\bullet. The invariant at stage n: F^i=0 for i<n, and for every j, H^i(\alpha_{f_j}) is an isomorphism for i>n and surjective for i=n. Start: by step 2 each M^\bullet_{f_j} has cohomology vanishing in large degrees, so choose n with H^i(M^\bullet_{f_j})=0 for all i\ge n and all j, and take F^\bullet=0. Step: let C^\bullet=\operatorname{Cone}(\alpha); localization is exact and commutes with cones, so the long exact cohomology sequence of F^\bullet_{f_j}\to M^\bullet_{f_j}\to C^\bullet_{f_j}\to F^\bullet_{f_j}[1] gives H^i(C^\bullet_{f_j})=0 for i\ge n. In the sense of [lem-sc-cone-pseudo-coherent], F^\bullet_{f_j} is a bounded complex of finite free A_{f_j}-modules, hence m-pseudo-coherent for every m (identity map), and M^\bullet_{f_j} is (n-1)-pseudo-coherent: if P^\bullet is the bounded-above finite-free model of step 2, the stupid truncation \sigma_{\ge n-1}P^\bullet\to P^\bullet\cong M^\bullet_{f_j} is an isomorphism on H^i for i>n-1 and surjective on H^{n-1}. Applying [lem-sc-cone-pseudo-coherent] with m=n-1 to this triangle, C^\bullet_{f_j} is (n-1)-pseudo-coherent, and [lem-sc-finite-cohomology] with m=n-1 gives that H^{n-1}(C^\bullet_{f_j}) is a finite A_{f_j}-module.

source.place: Tag 08EE proof, induction setup and cone paragraph

proof.text: For each j choose finitely many classes generating H^{n-1}(C^\bullet_{f_j}), represent them by elements of C^{n-1}_{f_j}, and multiply by a common power of f_j so that all representatives come from C^{n-1}. Take the direct sum of the resulting finite free A-modules over all j. Since each representative is a cocycle after localization, multiply the corresponding basis vector by a further power of f_j so that its composite to C^n is zero in C^n; one common power for all finitely many vectors gives a map \beta:F^{n-1}\to C^{n-1} whose composite to C^n is zero and whose localization surjects onto H^{n-1}(C^\bullet_{f_j}) for every j (the powers are units after localization, and the summands for other indices still land in cocycles). Writing C^{n-1}=M^{n-1}\oplus F^n, the components of \beta define the next component \alpha^{n-1} of \alpha and the differential F^{n-1}\to F^n. The zero composite makes these maps a morphism of complexes, and the induced morphism from the triangle (F^{\ge n})\to(F^{\ge n-1})\to F^{n-1}[1-n] to the cone triangle, with the four and five lemmas, shows that the new map induces isomorphisms on localized cohomology in degrees at least n and a surjection in degree n-1, which is the invariant at stage n-1 (in degree n-1 it need not be injective yet; that is achieved at the next stage). Since the degrees i\ge n are never changed afterwards, the limit F^\bullet is bounded above with finite free terms and every \alpha_{f_j}:F^\bullet_{f_j}\to M^\bullet_{f_j} is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 08EE proof, induction step and denominator-clearing paragraph

proof.text: Termwise association gives a bounded-above complex of finite free \mathcal O_X-modules \widetilde{F^\bullet} and a map \widetilde\alpha:\widetilde{F^\bullet}\to\widetilde{M^\bullet}. Its restriction to each D(f_j) is \widetilde{\alpha_{f_j}}, a quasi-isomorphism by step 4 and exactness of localization; being a quasi-isomorphism is local, so \widetilde\alpha|_U is a quasi-isomorphism. Therefore \widetilde{F^\bullet}|_U\cong\widetilde{M^\bullet}|_U\cong E'|_U\cong E in D(\mathcal O_U).
